title: Maheshwari saree
summary: Maheshwari cloth comes from the town of Maheshwar on the Narmada river in Madhya Pradesh. It is a light handloom fabric with a cotton warp and a silk weft, woven in plain colour, in small checks or in stripes. Its borders are reversible, showing the same pattern on both faces of the cloth.
howToPlay: Pick a thread colour and a pattern shape from the tray.
Touch a square of the cloth to weave that shape there; it is mirrored into the other three corners of the design.
Copy the check and stripe pattern shown on the card, then press Check.
rules: The design is mirrored left to right and top to bottom, so every shape you place also appears on its partner squares.
A square counts only when its shape and its thread colour both match the pattern you are copying.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; you can undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: Weaving at Maheshwar is traditionally linked with the court of Ahilyabai Holkar in the 1700s, and the cloth is still woven on handlooms by families in the town. The checks echo the pattern of woven mats, and the reversible border is a mark of careful weaving.
